Removed bare 1-bit from the one-bit predictor aliases because it also describes ordinary bit widths; precise predictor/entry names remain.

authorCorrectionsIndependentlyReviewed: Added explicit grouping around unit-bearing denominators and complete units in standalone formula definitions/substitutions; use conventional implicit products for scalar power expressions.
Corrected the activity-factor convention: activity-weighted capacitance is aC, not C with activity counted twice; the bounded 0–1 approximation explicitly neglects extra intra-cycle glitches.
Corrected the single-cycle period inverse to divide by the whole picosecond quantity, and qualified long-run balanced-stage speedup rather than implying the finite-run gain equals stage count.
Removed misleading opposite glossary aliases: variable-length from fixed-length, unaligned from aligned, imprecise from precise exceptions, branch-likely from ordinary delay-slot behaviour.
Distinguished issue, decode, allocation and retirement widths rather than treating them as one 4-wide limit; ROB/physical result storage and store visibility no longer use one universal organisation.
Qualified load-use, forwarding and hazard stalls to the precise teaching timing and operand-consumption assumptions; newest unavailable loads must stall, not forward their addresses.
Qualified one-bit loop misses, predictor aliasing, branch recovery cost, branch-history indexing and return prediction; generic aliasing and window size cannot silently open the wrong definition.
Replaced universal power/voltage/frequency/accelerator/core-efficiency claims in inherited glossary definitions with scoped workload and implementation explanations.
Clarified that x86 REP MOVSB is one compact encoding of repeated work; instruction-event counting and internal work cannot be inferred from that encoding alone.
Identified the perf transcript as illustrative; never present its counters as measurements performed for the lesson.
Removed source-level claims that the ternary byte selection commonly must become CMOV; machine code and workload measurement determine the result.
Closed the hazard scheduling question fence on its own line so the following memory-order assumptions render as prose.
Replaced cross-question stage-delay context with explicit values in the standalone pipeline-latency question; all original answer keys remain unchanged.
Added useful comments to Python loops/state updates/renaming/readiness models and C/assembly examples; all original executable statements are retained.
Strengthened glossary links to fetched primary documentation and replaced a draft student-slide Gustafson citation with the original paper before handoff.

Original .md and .questions.json archives remain byte-identical.
